refs: Jer 29:1 , Jeremiah sends a letter to the captives in Babylon to be quiet there
Jer 29:8 , and not to believe the dreams of their prophets

Jer 29:15 , He foretells the destruction of the rest for their disobedience
Jer 29:20 , He shews the fearful end of Ahab and Zedekiah, two lying prophets
Jer 29:24 , Shemaiah writes a letter against Jeremiah

20.heading: hear:
refs: Dr. Blayney thinks there were two letters written by the prophet to the captives in Babylon, and the first ends with this verse. That having heard, on the return of the embassy, that the captives had received his advice favourably, and because they were deceived by false prophets, who promised them a speedier deliverance, he therefore wrote a second letter, beginning with the Jer 29:15 , and going on with the twenty-first, etc. - in which order these verses are read in the Septuagint in which he denounces God's judgments on the three chief of those, Ahab, Zedekiah, and Shemaiah.
